e713_scale.question: do the brake and the two-field dictionary hold at 7B: e697 (the brake) and e706 (the strong field) at Qwen2.5-7B, blocks 14 and 21 of 28, fp32, 40 neurons each?
B0: every input reproduces the neuron at 7B in fp32 (the all-inputs ratio under 0.05)
B1: the off-class positions carry at least 0.7 of the sixteen-input damage over all positions
B1b: the top-5 percent positions alone carry at most 0.3 of it
B2: sixteen excitatory plus sixteen inhibitory wires halve the sixteen-absolute wires' ratio at the firings
B2b: and beat thirty-two absolute wires by 0.1
B3: the weak bus halves the sixteen wires' ratio at the firings
B4: signed wires with the bus bring the ratio under 0.25
B5: the sixteen inhibitory wires carry at least half of the crowd's opposition
B6: the bus halves the all-position ratio
H0: every input reproduces the neuron (e706 at 7B)
H1: the strong field alone halves the sixteen-wire ratio at the firings
H2: weak and strong together beat the weak field alone by 0.1
H3: both fields with the attention units bring the ratio under 0.25
H5: both fields beat a random subspace of their dimension by 0.2
H6: both fields halve the all-position ratio
runs: e697_brake.py and e706_strong_field.py at qwen7b blocks 14 and 21, fp32, the scripts unchanged except the sample sizes: 32 evaluation windows and 48 held-out windows (the record's 64 and 96 did not fit 80 GB at 7B), 40 neurons

e714_fisher_dictionary.question: does choosing a position's k atoms by orthogonal matching pursuit in a blended metric, the output's Fisher (unit mean eigenvalue) plus lambda times the identity, recover more of the mean-ablation KL for the same k than the Euclidean pursuit, and does that metric prefer the field atoms?
F1: at k = 16 with rows and fields, the blended pursuit (lambda 1) recovers 0.1 more of the mean-ablation KL than the Euclidean pursuit
F2: its Fisher residual is lower by 0.2
F4: it chooses field atoms 0.1 more often
F5: with the fields in the dictionary it beats rows-only blended pursuit at 16 by 0.05
F6: sixteen blended-chosen atoms beat the stream's top sixteen principal directions
F7: sixteen blended-chosen atoms match thirty-two Euclidean-chosen ones
F8: the pure Fisher pursuit (lambda 0) recovers less than the Euclidean one: a diagnostic of the sampled Fisher's blind directions
runs: gpt2 b5, gpt2 b8, pythia160 b6, pythia410 b12, qwen05 b12, gpt2m b12; 256 positions per block, 128 scored by KL
